deposit_time.evidence: GaugeV2 was designed to enforce a cooldown (“maturity”) before liquidity can be withdrawn, protecting the protocol from mercenary farming and short-cycle reward extraction. The mechanism hinges on the `maturityTime` mapping: deposits should set `maturityTime[user] = block.timestamp + lockPeriod`, and withdrawals should revert until that time passes.

withdraw_time.evidence: The withdrawal path does include a `require(block.timestamp >= maturityTime[msg.sender], "!MATURE")`, but the deposit path never sets the mapping. Solidity’s default for a mapping value is zero, so the check always passes. Any user can therefore enter and exit the gauge instantly, capturing emissions without respecting the intended lock. This undermines the tokenomics assumptions documented under “Locks & Voting Power” and “G-1/G-2 invariants,” effectively nullifying the maturity design.
